tagline: A ferry crosses the Little Wicomico; menhaden shaped Reedville’s waterfront.
intro: On Northumberland County’s byways, Route 644 crosses the Little Wicomico River by ferry. The river is mostly tidal and meets the Chesapeake Bay at the Potomac’s southern shore. Virginia’s byway designation identifies scenic roads that introduce travelers to alternative destinations.

The ferry connection has its own interruptions and repairs. After service stopped in summer 2020, the Sunnybank vessel went into dry dock for cleaning and maintenance. New loading ramps were installed before service resumed that December.

Follow the documented ferry segment from Route 645 north of Ganyon, across the Little Wicomico, to Route 652 east of Beverlyville. Reedville stands at US 360’s eastern end on Cockrell’s Creek, with Victorian mansions built from fishing wealth. For a separate coastal excursion, Hughlett Point preserves wetlands, dunes, forest and undeveloped beach.

moments.title: Sunnybank Ferry
moments.text: At Sunnybank, the road connection across the Little Wicomico depends on a cable-guided ferry. It links Sunny Bank and Ferry roads across a river that is mostly tidal. In July 2020, VDOT took Sunnybank and Merry Point out of service ahead of expected bad weather. Sunnybank’s suspension continued through a maintenance project; its December return followed dry-dock work and the installation of new vehicle ramps. The river runs nine miles to the Chesapeake Bay. VDOT’s byway record includes the ferry crossing between Route 645 and Route 652.

moments.title: Reedville
moments.text: Menhaden paid for Reedville’s Main Street houses. Captain Elijah W. Reed arrived from Maine in 1874 and brought a method of rendering the fish in large quantities for oil. The oil served lighting and lubrication; bones and carcasses became fertilizer. The town remains a landing place for the fish: Omega Protein runs vessels from Reedville and brings much of its catch here. The historic district includes five modified Queen Anne houses known as Millionaires Row, a tangible result of the menhaden industry. The Reedville Fishermen’s Museum preserves the town’s watermen’s heritage and includes the restored Walker House, the community’s oldest home.

moments.title: Hughlett Point Natural Area Preserve
moments.text: Hughlett Point protects 204 acres of habitat, from tidal and non-tidal wetlands to dunes, upland forest and undeveloped beaches. It provides a staging area for migrating birds and habitat for the northeastern beach tiger beetle and other rare invertebrates. Trails, a boardwalk and a viewing platform form part of the preserve’s visitor facilities. Some shoreline areas have seasonal access restrictions to protect shorebirds and other sensitive species. The Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation owns and maintains the preserve. Educational signs accompany the trails and viewing facilities through these protected habitats.
